newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN UPSET ANDERLECHT IN BELGIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN UPSET ANDERLECHT IN BELGIAN CUP.

text.p: Unfancied Ekeren overcame a two-goal deficit to beat Anderlecht 4-2 after extra time and win their first Belgian Cup on Sunday.
It was only the third defeat in 11 cup final appearances for Anderlecht, who last lost in 1977 when Ekeren were still playing in one of the nation's lower regional divisions.
Ekeren, who beat Anderlecht 4-1 in a league match last month, had lost their two previous finals, in 1990 and 1995.
Canadian international Tomasz Radzinski and Gunther Hofmans scored the decisive goals in the first five minutes of extra time after Ekeren had fought back to snatch a 2-2 draw in normal time.
Anderlecht's Ukranian striker Oleg Yaschuk opened the scoring in the 31st minute with a glancing header from a corner.

Desperate to lift the cup to put some shine on a disappointing season, Anderlecht appeared to have the match sewn up in the 55th minute when Ghanaian defender Samuel Johnson beat Belgian goalkeeper Philippe Vande Walle with a low shot from 12 metres.
But Johnson turned villain just nine minutes later with a stunning, diving headed own goal.
Ekeren winger Christophe Kinet levelled in the 85th minute when he pounced on a rebound after Johnson had cleared a Cvijan Milosevic effort off the goal-line.
Anderlecht tried desperately to turn the tide in the dying minutes, with efforts from Johnson and Walem hitting the woodwork.
